# zone_dns_caa_record (Resource)

A `CAA` record, declaring which certificate authorities may issue for the domain.

~> **There is no `ttl` argument.** The zone.eu API does not expose a TTL on DNS records, so neither does this provider. TTLs are managed by zone.eu.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "zone_dns_caa_record" "letsencrypt" {
  zone        = "example.com"
  name        = "example.com"
  destination = "letsencrypt.org"
  tag         = "issue"
}

resource "zone_dns_caa_record" "report" {
  zone        = "example.com"
  name        = "example.com"
  destination = "mailto:security@example.com"
  tag         = "iodef"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `destination` (String) The property value, such as the CA's domain for an `issue` tag.
- `name` (String) The fully qualified record name, for example `www.example.com`. zone.eu stores names in full rather than relative to the zone, so a bare `www` is rejected. Use the zone name itself for a record at the apex.
- `tag` (String) The property being set: `issue`, `issuewild` or `iodef`.
- `zone` (String) The DNS zone holding this record, for example `example.com`. Zones are not created by this provider: one exists for each domain or hosting service on the account. Changing this forces a new record.

### Optional

- `flag` (Number) Flags byte. `0` is the usual value; `128` marks the property critical.

### Read-Only

- `comment` (String) Note attached to the record by zone.eu. Read-only.
- `deletable` (Boolean) Whether zone.eu allows this record to be removed. Records it manages itself report `false`, and a destroy of one will fail.
- `id` (Number) Numeric identifier assigned by zone.eu.
- `modifiable` (Boolean) Whether zone.eu allows this record to be changed. Records it manages itself report `false`, and an update to one will fail.
- `resource_url` (String) API URL of this record.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing record with "<zone>/<record id>".
# The record id appears in the resource_url of the zone_dns_records data source.
terraform import zone_dns_caa_record.example "example.com/12345"
```
